feeds.overview: The Consumer Engagement Analytics bundle contains data used in the Oracle Health Data Intelligence Consumer Engagement service.

files_summary.description: This table contains information about the venue addresses where the event is being held.
This table contains information about the consumers who attended each event and slot.
This table contains information about the category to which an event belongs.

This table contains information about an event category's code, which represents a concept from a single, specified (not fixed) code system. No restrictions exist for the code system. It can be local and proprietary or standard and recognized by Health Data Intelligence.
This table contains information about an event. This includes event details such as the name, start time, end time, and multiple slot information.
This table contains information about the individual who will provide guidance and instructions for the event.
This table contains information about the event's location.
This table contains registration information. A registration defines which consumer registered for which slot, event, and series.
This table contains information about an event series. An event series groups related events.

This table contains information about an event's slot. It contains details such as the number of available registrations, the maximum registration limit, the cutoff time for registration, the slot starting time, and the slot ending time.
This table contains the contact details of the person who is assigned as the leader of the event or series.

This table contains information about the name of a person. This includes name information for people in the PH_D_Person table and for people not in the PH_D_Person table.
This table contains information about phone numbers for a person. There is phone number information for people in the PH_D_Person table and for people not in the PH_D_Person table.
This table has person race information. There is race information for people in PH_D_Person table and for people not in the PH_D_Person table.
This table contains information about subpopulations that are defined for a person. For example, a subpopulation could be Healthe Registries.
This table contains title information for a person. There is title information for people in the PH_D_Person table and for people not in the PH_D_Person table.
This table contains given name information for a provider in activity data. It also includes demographic information for providers included in the data and provides links to personnel.
This table contains data used to populate cost and utilization data, such as per member per month (PMPM). This table identifies if a member has been covered for a certain month.
This table contains information on person-centric advance directive data.

This table contains person-centric allergy data. If the allergy update is linked to an encounter, the EncounterID field is populated. If there is more than one reaction for an allergy, multiple records are sent for each reaction. Each record should contain the same allergy-level field values, such as AllergyID, Version, PersonID, EncounterID, and so on. The reaction-level fields, such as ReactionCodeID, ReactionCodeSystemID, ReactionDisplay, SeverityCodeID, SeverityCodeSystemID, and SeverityDisplay should be different.
This table contains comment data for the person-centric allergy data.
The table contains information about the provenance agent for the allergy.

This table contains information on allergy reactions. Each record should contain the same allergy-level field values but the reaction-level fields such as ReactionCodeID, ReactionCodeSystemID, ReactionDisplay, SeverityCodeID, SeverityCodeSystemID, and SeverityDisplay should be different.

This table contains information about the appointment where a health care service may take place or has already taken place. Examples include a scheduled surgery, a follow-up for a clinical visit, a scheduled conference call between clinicians to discuss a case, the reservation of a piece of diagnostic equipment for a particular use, and so on. The visit scheduled by an appointment can be in person or remote.
This table contains additional information on appointments with actions.
This table contains additional information on an appointment with the participants information.

This table contains information about appointment slots. This includes the time and usage of one or more individuals, locations, and pieces of equipment being reserved for a designated period of time. An appointment is about a person, but the person may not be a required attendee. In some instances, an appointment can be scheduled without a slot.
This table contains detailed information about appointment information.
This table contains calculated risk assessment information that is generated by the platform for a given population.
This table contains the calculated risk assessment covariate value, name, and sequence information.
This table contains the supporting facts that are used to create the risk assessment covariate.
This table contains the calculated risk assessment child covariate value, name, and sequence information.
This table contains the supporting facts that are used to create the risk assessment child covariate.

This table contains the care plans that describe how providers intend to deliver care for a person. Care plans can have a variety of scopes. A care plan can be as simple as tracking follow-up appointments, or facilitating education for a person.
This table contains activity and goal relationships that have been identified in the care plan.
This table contains the codified values for any care plan activities identified in the care plan.
This table contains any comments associated with the care plan activities.
This table contains any care plan barriers that have been identified for the delivery of care to the person.
This table contains the goals identified for the person on the care plan.
This table contains any comments associated with the care plan goal.
This table contains the providers identified for the person on the care plan.
This table contains information to help define the care team, such as start and end date descriptions and the type of care team it is.
This table contains the identifier for the individual care team participants.
This table contains details about the prevenance agent related to the care team.
This table contains the claim information. This is at a heading level and only contains the information that pertains to the claim as a whole.
This table contains the codes associated with the claims. It also contains detailed information about the claim code including the raw code, the claim code primary display, and more.
This table contains the claim information. This contains the details for each service line of the claim. The data listed is only associated with the line number listed in the table.
This table contains detailed claim information and gives information regarding adjustments.
This table contains diagnoses associated with records from the PH_F_Claim_Detail table. For example, the set of diagnoses associated with a given claim service line.
This claims table contains the drug ingredient numerator and denominator for medications, such as drug codes, displays, strengths, and more.
This table contains the claim subscriber information. This is at a heading level and only contains information that pertains to the claim as a whole.
This table contains diagnoses associated with the records from the PH_F_Claim_Detail table. This table contains the plan ID from the claim data.
This table contains the principal procedure modifier code.
This table contains the procedure modifier code.

feeds.overview: The Millennium operational data store (ODS) bundle contains 1217 files that represent the data from the Cerner Millennium domain.

files_summary.description: Encounter based table for ProFile Chart Abstracting information
Abstract data
Flexing options for order entry formats.
Every accession number generated by the system will be represented by a row in this table.
This table contains a single record of the summary for the external accession assigned to the contents of an accession in Millennium
The resolution table between accessions and orders. This table will tell you what orders belong to an accession. It will also tell you what accession(s) an order belongs to.
The account table will hold information about internal organization accounts as well as patient accounts

This table stores the default behaviors for all accounts that are created based on this template. An account template is only owned by one billing entity and cannot be used to create accounts for other billing entities.
Item / Location relationship that defines how you acquire an item.

This table stores a high level view of all activity as it enters the system. An activity can be either a transaction (payment, write off, adjustment, charge) or correspondence, (bill, claim, letter,fax, email, phone call)
Pathway components on the activity data model
act pw comp focus r
Used to define groups of components within a pathway.
A record of actions performed on activity component groups.
Used to define relationships between pathway components.

The address table contains all addresses. An address table row is associated with a row in another table (i.e., person). Each address row is identified by the name of the table it is related to & the related table's primary row identifier.
Tracks modifications to history elements for a given address table.
Stores parameters used for advanced delta checking for General Lab applications
The alias pool table contains information about unique sets of numbers that are used for identification of different entities (I.e., persons, personnel, organizations, encounters, etc.).
The Allergy table contains coded and freetext allergic reaction and adverse effect information about a person
Allows comments to be added to adverse effects and allergic reactions.
Used to store codified alpha responses for discrete task assays that are result type of alpha.
Allows categorization of Alpha Responses.
Contains rules related to a given alpha response.
Used to store alternate search categories or items. (i.e. PowerOrders favorites and favorite folders)
Alternate Selection List. Contains the parent-child associations between alternate selection categories and other categories, synonyms, home-health problems and reference tasks.
Contains APC vocabulary specific data.

When a user activates an application, a context is created that represents a unique occurrence of the application being activated by that user. The context is associated with a unique number that can be used to identify other rows that have been modified or created during that context. The context number is recorded in the column UPDT_APPLCTX on most tables.
This table contains application level preferences for PowerChart. The table is structured so that other applications should be able to use it.
This table maintains a list of synoptic worksheets associated with an Anatomic Pathology case.

This reference table contains entries representing diagnostic correlation discrepancy categorizations. This option is most often associated with diagnostic correlation evaluation terms that represent disagreement.
This reference table includes the terminology used to designate agreement or disagreement for a diagnostic correlation event.

This activity table includes an entry for every diagnostic correlation event that has been established, regardless of whether or not the evaluation has simply been initiated, is in process, is complete, or is canceled.

This reference table includes the parameters established for diagnostic correlation studies. Every study contains parameters regarding a specific set of events or information to be evaluated and correlated.
This activity table contains the quality assurance indicators associated with gynecologic cytology cases. Indicators include classifications such as normal, atypical, abnormal, and unsatisfactory.

This reference table contains the individual specimen, block/cassette, and slide identification scheme values. For example, the values 1, 2, and 3 would be included on this table if a numeric scheme has been defined for association with a prefix.
Stores relationships for assays and the service resources that perform them. Used to store service resource specific information about task/assays used for result entry parameters
Contains a record for every time a product was assigned (or reserved) to a person.
Contains a record of every time an assignment was released from a person.
Account Template Account Relation
Stores information that indicates special authorizations for particular visits or procedures under a health plan's coverage
Store detail information related to an authorization/referral
Contains a record of every time an autologous or directed product was associated with a person.
Detail for the batch denial file table
Relates the batches and denial codes.
Media that need to be printed in a batch run
Contains information about a Batch Transaction
Holds all of the transaction data whether it gets posted or not.
Contains information about a Batch Transaction File
Holds the relationship between a batch and a transaction

This activity table is a smaller version of the Product table, and is intended to store products loaded in from previous systems. It will also be used in the future to store purged products from the live inventory.(from the Product table).
This activity table is a smaller version of the Product_Event table, and is intended to store disposition information on products loaded in from previous systems.
This table is used to store antigens from a product history upload.
Contains a row for each autologous or directed product for which an allogeneic product was dispensed to the same patient (by overriding the exception).
Any device to which the blood bank may dispense blood that is kept at a controlled temperature.
Used to record the transfer of a product from one device to another while product is dispensed.
This table contains override information for discrepancies that occurred with an Electronic Delivery Note file import.
This table contains the product information from an Electronic Delivery Note message structure.
Blood Bank Computer Crossmatch Exception Product

feeds.overview: The Wellness Campaign Analytics bundle contains data about wellness campaigns for a tenant.

files_summary.description: This table contains the version records of a campaign. These version records are also known as instances or configurations. A wellness campaign is an incentive program designed to motivate members to improve their health by completing incentivized activities. A campaign is an organized collection of incentivized activities grouped into categories, subcategories, and groups. A category can have subcategories and a subcategory can have groups. A campaign instance is generated using all the configuration data.
This table contains category definitions across all instances of wellness campaigns.
This table contains all the campaign-to-consumer mappings that were deleted.
This table contains the campaign-to-consumer mappings.
This table contains the details of all populations across all instances of wellness campaigns.

Participation in a wellness campaign is incentivized through rewards (also known as points). This table contains the details of adjustment rewards across all instances of wellness campaigns and their categories.

Wellness campaigns define objectives (also known as goals) for a consumer to complete to make them eligible for earning rewards. This table contains the details of all the alternative objectives across all instances of wellness campaigns and their categories.
Primary objectives (also known as goals) for categories in wellness campaigns have incentives. This table contains the details of the incentives associated with primary objectives.
This table contains all reward-to-consumer mappings. Rewards are also known as points.

Wellness campaigns define objectives (also known as goals) for a consumer to complete to make them eligible for earning rewards. This table contains the details of all the primary objectives across all instances of wellness campaigns and their categories.

Participation in a wellness campaign is incentivized through rewards (also known as points). This table contains the details of rewards across all instances of wellness campaigns and their categories.
Objectives (also known as goals) can have exemptions defined for them. This table contains details of exemptions awarded to consumers across all instances of wellness campaigns.
This table contains details to support consumer objectives (also known as goals) across all instances of wellness campaigns.
This table contains all instances of consumers' fulfillment of objectives (also known as goals).
This table contains all instance of consumers' incentives.
This table contains definitions for objectives' (also known as goals) completion criteria across all objectives.
This table contains details of the acceptable sources across all objectives (also known as goals).
This table contains all instances of consumers' overall fulfillment of objectives (also known as goals).
This table contains details to support consumer rewards (also known as points) across all instances of wellness campaigns.
